scenes.title: The Woman
scenes.summary: Watson introduces Irene Adler as 'the woman' who alone eclipses Holmes's cold, reasoning mind, and recalls his own drifting apart from Holmes into married life while Holmes pursues crime between cocaine and ambition.

scenes.title: Reunion and Deduction
scenes.summary: Watson visits Baker Street on March 20, 1888, finds Holmes pacing over a new problem, and endures Holmes's playful deductions about his weight, practice, wet shoes and servant, leading to the lesson: you see but do not observe.

scenes.title: The Masked Summons
scenes.summary: Holmes shares a masked visitor's mysterious note; by paper watermark and German phrasing they trace it to Bohemia, then hear a brougham arrive and Holmes insists Watson stay as his Boswell.

scenes.title: The King Unmasked
scenes.summary: A gigantic masked nobleman calling himself Count Von Kramm demands secrecy, admits he serves the House of Ormstein, and when pressed tears off his mask to reveal he is the hereditary King of Bohemia himself.

scenes.title: The Compromising Photograph
scenes.summary: The King confesses his five-year-old entanglement in Warsaw with opera singer Irene Adler, compromising letters and a cabinet photograph together, and admits bribes, burglaries and waylayings have all failed to recover it.

scenes.title: Three Days to Ruin
scenes.summary: Irene threatens to send the photograph to the King's puritanical fiancee on betrothal day next Monday, leaving three days; Holmes yawns, promises to act, and learns she has a soul of steel.

scenes.title: Carte Blanche
scenes.summary: The King at the Langham offers carte blanche and 1000 pounds, gives Briony Lodge as Irene's address, and leaves in his brougham while Holmes asks Watson to return tomorrow at three to discuss the case.

scenes.title: A Groom Out of Work
scenes.summary: Holmes returns to Baker Street disguised as a drunken groom and reports his morning's work: surveying Briony Lodge and learning from the Serpentine-mews ostlers that Irene Adler lives quietly but receives daily visits from lawyer Godfrey Norton, leaving the location of the photograph in doubt.

scenes.title: A Hasty Wedding
scenes.summary: Holmes watches Norton and then Adler rush off in separate cabs to the Church of St. Monica, follows them himself, and is seized inside as a makeshift witness to their sudden marriage before the couple separate again.

scenes.title: Enlisting Watson
scenes.summary: Over cold beef and beer, Holmes warns his plans are menaced by the marriage and secures Watson's delighted promise to help, even to break the law and risk arrest for an excellent cause.

scenes.title: The Smoke Rocket Plot
scenes.summary: Holmes details the smoke-rocket fire-cry scheme: Watson must stay neutral, watch from the sitting-room window, and throw the rocket on signal, then Holmes transforms into a benevolent Nonconformist clergyman.

scenes.title: Dusk Watch Before Briony Lodge
scenes.summary: At dusk Holmes and Watson wait before Briony Lodge in Serpentine Avenue, noting the house and the remarkably animated street with loafers, guardsmen, and loungers gathered nearby.

scenes.title: Where the Photograph Must Lie
scenes.summary: As they pace before the house, Holmes reasons that the marriage makes the photograph a double-edged weapon, and that Irene must keep it in her own house where she can seize it at once, not on her person or with banker or lawyer.

scenes.title: The Staged Quarrel
scenes.summary: Holmes vows to make Irene show him the hiding-place; as her landau arrives his hired loafers stage a savage quarrel, and Holmes falls bleeding to gain sympathy and entry while Irene watches from the steps.

scenes.title: Fire!
scenes.summary: Carried solicitously to the sofa by the kind Irene, Holmes signals for air; Watson tosses the rocket crying Fire, smoke fills the room amid general panic, and the friends slip away to the corner of the street.

scenes.title: Where She Rushed
scenes.summary: Laughing, Holmes explains the old trick: thinking her house afire, Irene rushed to the recess behind the sliding panel above the bell-pull, revealing the hiding place; they will return with the King at eight next morning.

scenes.title: Good-night, Mr. Holmes
scenes.summary: Searching for his key at Baker Street door, Holmes is hailed by a slim youth in an ulster with a strangely familiar voice, leaving him wondering who the deuce it could have been.

scenes.title: Morning of Expectation
scenes.summary: After sleeping at Baker Street, Watson and Holmes are burst in upon by the impatient King demanding the photograph; reassured only with hopes, they take his waiting brougham back to Briony Lodge.

scenes.title: She Is Married
scenes.summary: In the carriage Holmes drops that Irene married English lawyer Norton yesterday; the King laments her lost queenship while Holmes hopes love for her husband will end the threat to the royal marriage.

scenes.title: The Letter
scenes.summary: Briony Lodge is ransacked and empty, fled to the Continent; behind the shutter Holmes finds only Irene's own photograph and her midnight letter confessing she followed him disguised in male costume and keeps the original only as safeguard.

scenes.title: Her Word Is Inviolable
scenes.summary: The King marvels at Irene Adler's quickness and resolution, Holmes coldly replies she is on a very different level, and the King calls the outcome most successful because her word is inviolate and the photograph is as safe as if in the fire.

scenes.title: The Woman
scenes.summary: The King offers Holmes an emerald snake ring as reward, Holmes asks instead for Irene's photograph and departs, and Watson closes that Holmes's best plans were beaten by a woman's wit and that he ever after speaks of her as the woman.

scenes.title: The Red-Headed Visitor
scenes.summary: Watson visits Holmes and finds him with a fiery red-headed client. Holmes insists Watson stay to hear what promises to be a singular and possibly unique case.

scenes.title: Holmes Reads Wilson
scenes.summary: Holmes amuses Watson by deducing Wilson's manual labour, snuff, Freemasonry, China stay, and writing from his hands, clothes, tattoo, and watch-chain.

scenes.title: The Extraordinary Advertisement
scenes.summary: Wilson produces the newspaper advertisement for the Red-Headed League offering £4 a week for nominal services, astonishing Watson and delighting Holmes.

scenes.title: Spaulding's Tempting Suggestion
scenes.summary: Wilson describes his quiet pawnbroker household, his cheap assistant Spaulding, and how Spaulding urged him to apply for the League founded by Ezekiah Hopkins.

scenes.title: The Crowd at Pope's Court
scenes.summary: Wilson recalls Fleet Street choked with red-headed applicants of every shade answering the advertisement, and how Spaulding pushed, pulled, and butted through the crowd and up the stairs to get him into the office.

scenes.title: Duncan Ross Tests the Hair
scenes.summary: In the bare office Duncan Ross favours Wilson, examines his hair and violently tugs it to prove it genuine, dismisses the crowd, introduces himself, waives the objection to Wilson being a bachelor, and sets the hours at ten to two, which Spaulding offers to cover the shop for.

scenes.title: Copying the Encyclopaedia
scenes.summary: Wilson accepts £4 a week to copy the Encyclopaedia Britannica from ten to two without leaving, and works diligently for eight weeks until Duncan Ross stops appearing.

scenes.title: The Cardboard Notice
scenes.summary: Wilson shows the cardboard notice dissolving the Red-Headed League, prompting Holmes and Watson to burst into laughter.

scenes.title: The Vanished Men
scenes.summary: Chastened, Wilson recounts asking neighbours and the landlord, learning Ross was William Morris who moved out, and finding only a knee-cap factory at his given address.

scenes.title: Questions About the Assistant
scenes.summary: Holmes questions Wilson closely about his assistant's wages, appearance, acid stain, and pierced ear, showing sudden excitement and promising an opinion by Monday.

scenes.title: A Three-Pipe Problem
scenes.summary: Alone with Watson, Holmes calls it a bizarre but not mysterious problem, falls into a fifty-minute pipe-smoking meditation, then proposes a City errand and concert.

scenes.title: Reconnaissance in Coburg Square
scenes.summary: Holmes inspects the pawnshop in Saxe-Coburg Square, tests the pavement with his stick, glimpses Spaulding's trouser knees, then notes the bank abutting behind.

scenes.title: Music and a Midnight Summons
scenes.summary: After an afternoon lost in Sarasate's violin music, Holmes warns of a considerable crime in contemplation and asks Watson to come armed at ten that night.

scenes.title: Assembling the Night Party
scenes.summary: Watson joins Holmes, police agent Jones, and bank director Merryweather at Baker Street to hunt the daring criminal John Clay over a high-stakes robbery.

scenes.title: Vigil in the Bank Vault
scenes.summary: Hidden in the bank's cellar of French gold, the four men extinguish their lantern and wait in cold darkness for the tunnelers to break through from Coburg Square.

scenes.title: The Tunnel Break-In
scenes.summary: The floor is breached and two thieves emerge; Holmes and Jones seize the red-headed accomplice's coat and capture John Clay after knocking his pistol aside.

scenes.title: Holmes Explains the Plot
scenes.summary: Back in Baker Street Holmes explains the League was a ploy to keep Wilson away while Clay tunnelled to the bank, timed for Saturday night, closing his ennui for a time.

scenes.title: Life Stranger Than Fiction
scenes.summary: Holmes and Watson debate by the Baker Street fire whether real life is stranger than fiction, testing newspaper cases. Holmes recalls souvenirs from the King of Bohemia and Holland and admits his current cases are important but uninteresting, until he spots a hesitant client in the street below.

scenes.title: Oscillation on the Pavement
scenes.summary: A large nervous woman with a fur boa and red feather oscillates on the pavement opposite. Holmes reads it as a perplexed love affair, not anger, and moments later she is announced as Miss Mary Sutherland.

scenes.title: The Typewritist Consults Holmes
scenes.summary: Holmes astonishes Mary by deducing her short sight and typewriting. She explains she sought him after Mrs. Etherege's case to find Mr. Hosmer Angel, defying her stepfather Mr. Windibank. Holmes probes her family: her mother's remarriage, the sold plumbing business, and her own New Zealand stock income controlled by Windibank.

scenes.title: Courtship of Hosmer Angel
scenes.summary: Mary recounts meeting Hosmer Angel at the gasfitters' ball against Windibank's wishes, their walks and engagement, his absence when her stepfather is home, daily letters to Leadenhall Street Post Office, his refusal of typewriting, and his shy manner, whispering voice, weak throat, and tinted glasses.

scenes.title: Vanished at the Church Door
scenes.summary: After Windibank returns to France, Angel proposes a secret wedding before his return and exacts Testament vows of fidelity whatever happens. On the wedding Friday at St. Saviour's, Angel vanishes from a four-wheeler en route. Mary believes catastrophe befell him; her mother forbids talk and her stepfather professes sympathy.

scenes.title: A Sealed Book
scenes.summary: Holmes promises to investigate but urges Mary to let Hosmer Angel vanish from memory. She insists she will remain true to him. She leaves her advertisement, four letters, and addresses, compelling Holmes's respect despite her vacuous manner.

scenes.title: Sleeves, Boots, and Typewriting
scenes.summary: Alone with Watson, Holmes smokes and calls the case trite but the maiden instructive. He lectures on sleeves, plush marks, pince-nez dents, odd half-buttoned boots, and violet ink, then examines the missing notice and typewritten letters, noting the typewritten signature as conclusive. He writes to the City firm and to Windibank.

scenes.title: Bisulphate of Baryta
scenes.summary: Watson, confident in Holmes after past successes, returns next evening after a grave medical case. He finds Holmes drowsy among chemical bottles smelling of hydrochloric acid, who claims there was never mystery but no law can touch the scoundrel who deserted Miss Sutherland.

scenes.title: The Typewriter's Individuality
scenes.summary: James Windibank arrives for his six o'clock appointment, deprecating publicity and calling the search for Hosmer Angel useless expense. Holmes claims he will succeed in finding Angel, then confronts Windibank with typewriter evidence: his own letter and Angel's four letters share the same slurred e's, tailless r's, and fourteen other identical defects.

scenes.title: The Locked Door Trap
scenes.summary: Windibank springs up to leave, but Holmes turns the key in the door and announces he has caught the man. Trapped and white-faced, Windibank collapses as Holmes calls the trick transparent, cruel and heartless, and prepares to run over the course of events.

scenes.title: The Angel Deception Exposed
scenes.summary: Holmes lays out the scheme: Windibank married for money and to keep Mary's hundred a year disguised himself as Hosmer Angel with tinted glasses, whiskers, and a whisper, won her affections, then ended it at the church with the four-wheeler trick to bind her for years.

scenes.title: Threat and Flight
scenes.summary: Windibank claims it was only a joke and threatens Holmes with assault for locking the door; Holmes releases him, reaches for a hunting crop to punish him, and Windibank flees down the road.

scenes.title: Voilà Tout
scenes.summary: Holmes calls Windibank a cold-blooded scoundrel bound for the gallows. He explains his reasoning — profit motive, never together, disguise hints, familiar handwriting avoided — verified via Westhouse & Marbank and typewritten reply. He declines to disillusion Mary, quoting Hafiz on snatching a delusion from a woman.

scenes.title: A Telegram from Holmes
scenes.summary: At breakfast Watson receives Holmes's telegram asking him to join the Boscombe Valley case. His wife urges him to go, and he rushes to Paddington where Holmes is pacing the platform.

scenes.title: The Case on the Train
scenes.summary: Alone in the train carriage, Holmes briefs Watson from the papers: old McCarthy found murdered by Boscombe Pool, evidence damning his son James, Lestrade retained by the believing Miss Turner. Holmes muses on circumstantial evidence and observation.

scenes.title: What the Accused Says
scenes.summary: Watson notes men have hanged on slighter evidence. Holmes offers James McCarthy's own newspaper statement for Watson to read.

scenes.title: The Son's Testimony
scenes.summary: James recounts returning from Bristol, following the 'Cooee' signal to the pool, quarrelling with his violent father, leaving him, then running back to find him dying mumbling about a rat and refusing to explain the quarrel.

scenes.title: The Vanishing Grey Cloth
scenes.summary: Pressed about the cry and a vanished grey cloth seen near the body, James remains vague. Watson sees a damning case, but Holmes declares he will assume the lad tells the truth and says no more until the scene.

scenes.title: Arrival at Ross
scenes.summary: Arriving at Ross, they are met by Lestrade and take rooms at the Hereford Arms. Lestrade offers a carriage to the scene, but Holmes, citing the fine barometer, declines to go that night.

scenes.title: A Passionate Protestation
scenes.summary: Miss Turner rushes impulsively into the room and appeals to Holmes, insisting from lifelong knowledge that James McCarthy is too tender-hearted to commit murder and could not be guilty.

scenes.title: The Cause of the Quarrel
scenes.summary: Miss Turner reveals James hid the quarrel to protect her: old McCarthy wanted James to marry her against the wishes of James and her father. Holmes learns Turner is gravely ill and connected to McCarthy in Victoria, then promises to reassure James.

scenes.title: Resolve to Visit the Prisoner
scenes.summary: Lestrade calls Holmes's hopes cruel, but Holmes says he sees his way to clear James. He arranges to visit James in Hereford prison that night while Watson waits at the hotel.

scenes.title: Evening Reflections and a Secret Marriage
scenes.summary: Alone, Watson puzzles over the back-wound, the rat reference, and the grey cloth. Holmes returns late revealing James's secret Bristol barmaid marriage, his motive for quarrelling, and fixes on the 'Cooee' and appointment as crucial.

scenes.title: Drive to Hatherley Farm
scenes.summary: Next bright morning they drive to Hatherley Farm. Lestrade reports Turner is dying. Holmes notes Turner's rent-free kindness to McCarthy makes McCarthy's confident marriage scheme singular, sparring with Lestrade over moonshine and fog.

scenes.title: Hunting Tracks at Boscombe Pool
scenes.summary: After measuring boots at the farm, Holmes races along the track to Boscombe Pool, nose to the ground like a hound, reading trampled grass, tiptoe tracks, and tracing a path to a great beech and the high road.

scenes.title: The Stone and the Description
scenes.summary: Back at the cab Holmes produces a mossy stone as the murder weapon and profiles the killer: tall, left-handed, limping, in shooting-boots and grey cloak, smoking Indian cigars. Lestrade scoffs as Holmes declares the mystery solved.

scenes.title: Cooee and Ballarat
scenes.summary: Over lunch Holmes expounds: the 'Cooee' was an Australian call meant not for the Bristol-absent son but for an Australian appointee, and the dying 'rat' was part of 'Ballarat' on the Victoria map — pointing to an Australian from Ballarat in a grey cloak.

scenes.title: Deduction Complete
scenes.summary: Holmes details the footprint lameness, the left-hand blow from behind the tree, the Indian cigar ash, holder and blunt pen-knife. As Watson names the culprit, the waiter ushers in Mr. John Turner himself.

scenes.title: The Dying Visitor
scenes.summary: The giant, ash-white, dying Turner limps in. Holmes confronts him gently: he knows all about McCarthy. Turner fears for Alice but promises he would have spoken to save James, agreeing to sign a written confession for extreme need.

scenes.title: Confession of Black Jack
scenes.summary: Turner confesses: once Black Jack of the Ballarat Gang, spared McCarthy's life, then blackmailed for twenty years with rent-free land and money. When McCarthy demanded Alice for his son, Turner waited behind the tree and struck him down, fleeing then returning for his dropped cloak.

scenes.title: Mercy and Acquittal
scenes.summary: Holmes pities Turner, promising to use the confession only to save McCarthy and otherwise keep his secret. Turner stumbles out, Holmes reflects on fate, and James is acquitted, Turner dying months later.

scenes.title: Records and Storm
scenes.summary: Watson introduces his case records from 1882-1890 and explains why he chose this unsolved affair, then sets the scene on a violent equinoctial storm evening in late September at Baker Street with Holmes cross-indexing and Watson reading.

scenes.title: A Bell in the Gale
scenes.summary: Hearing the bell in the storm, Watson and Holmes speculate on a visitor. Holmes admits he has no friends and expects a serious client, then invites the wet stranger in and deduces he has come from Horsham in the south-west.

scenes.title: The Client Introduced
scenes.summary: The young visitor reveals he was sent by Major Prendergast of the Tankerville case. Holmes modestly admits past defeats, and Openshaw promises a family chain of events more mysterious than anything in Holmes's experience.

scenes.title: The Uncle's Terror
scenes.summary: John Openshaw recounts his Confederate Colonel uncle Elias living reclusively at Horsham, the locked attic room, and the terror caused by a Pondicherry letter containing five orange pips and K.K.K., followed by burning papers, a new will, drunken terror, and death by drowning.

scenes.title: Father Follows Son
scenes.summary: Holmes notes the dates of threat and death. Openshaw continues: his father inherited Horsham, received a Dundee letter with pips ordering papers put on the sundial, died in a chalk-pit fall, and after nearly three years of peace Openshaw himself has now received the same warning.

scenes.title: The Envelope with Five Pips
scenes.summary: Openshaw shakes five dried orange pips from a London-postmarked envelope bearing K.K.K. and the sundial order. Helpless with fear, he admits doing nothing, and says police dismissed the warnings as jokes and left only a policeman in the house, to Holmes's fury.

scenes.title: The Blue-Tinted Paper
scenes.summary: Openshaw produces a discoloured blue-tinted sheet found on his uncle's floor, recalling such margins among the burned papers. In his uncle's hand and mentioning pips, he believes it a surviving page from a private diary.

scenes.title: The Diary Leaf and Urgent Orders
scenes.summary: Holmes examines the torn March 1869 diary leaf naming McCauley, Paramore, and John Swain and orders Openshaw to replace it in the brass box with a note that the rest were burned, set it on the sundial, and hurry home by the crowded Waterloo train without seeking revenge yet.

scenes.title: Armed Departure Into the Storm
scenes.summary: Assured Openshaw is armed, Holmes says he will work the case from London rather than Horsham and arranges a return visit in a day or two, as their visitor departs back into the storm.

scenes.title: The Ideal Reasoner
scenes.summary: Left alone after Openshaw departs into the storm, Holmes muses on the fantastic nature of the case and expounds the ideal reasoner who deduces past and future from a single fact. Recalling his stocked brain-attic, he takes down the encyclopaedia and begins his chain: Elias Openshaw must have fled America from fear, and the Pondicherry, Dundee and East London postmarks show the writers were aboard a ship.

scenes.title: The Deadly Urgency from London
scenes.summary: Holmes argues the seven weeks between the Pondicherry warning and death, against only days from Dundee, proves the pursuers follow their mailed K.K.K. tokens by sailing-ship while letters travel by mail-boat. Since this latest warning comes from London, no delay can be counted upon, making Openshaw's danger immediate and deadly.

scenes.title: The Ku Klux Klan
scenes.summary: Holmes concludes multiple determined men want the papers and that K.K.K. is a society's badge, not a man's initials. Reading the encyclopedia on the Ku Klux Klan, its pip warnings and 1869 collapse, he links Openshaw's stolen register to Southern vengeance.

scenes.title: Too Late
scenes.summary: On a cleared morning Holmes leaves early on the case while Watson reads the paper. The headline Tragedy Near Waterloo Bridge reports Openshaw's drowned body recovered after a cry and splash, ruled an accident on the way to the last train.

scenes.title: Holmes Turns Hunter
scenes.summary: Shaken and shamed at sending his client to death, Holmes vows personal revenge and spends the day out. Returning starving late at night, he triumphantly prepares five orange pips in an envelope addressed to Captain James Calhoun of the barque Lone Star.

scenes.title: The Lone Star Lost
scenes.summary: Holmes explains tracing the Lone Star through Pondicherry, Dundee, and London Lloyd's records, now sailed for Savannah with three Americans aboard. He has cabled Savannah police, but gales wreck the ship, leaving only a stern-post marked L.S. in the Atlantic.

scenes.title: The Slave to the Drug
scenes.summary: Watson describes Isa Whitney's long opium addiction and ruin. Late one night in June '89, a veiled lady bursts into Watson's sitting-room and throws herself sobbing on Mrs. Watson's shoulder, revealing herself as Kate Whitney, an old school friend of his wife.

scenes.title: The Missing Two Days
scenes.summary: Kate Whitney begs for the doctor's help: her husband Isa has not been home for two days. She believes he is lying in an East End opium den, the Bar of Gold in Upper Swandam Lane, and she fears to fetch him herself from among the ruffians there.

scenes.title: The Promise to Go Alone
scenes.summary: Watson, as Isa Whitney's medical adviser, promises Kate he will go alone and send her husband home in a cab within two hours. He leaves his cheery sitting-room at once, speeding eastward by hansom on a strange errand.

scenes.title: The Opium Den
scenes.summary: Watson descends into the squalid, smoke-filled opium den in Upper Swandam Lane. Amid stupor and muttering addicts he finds a haggard Isa Whitney, confused about the day, and prepares to send him home.

scenes.title: Holmes Unmasked
scenes.summary: The aged addict by the brazier is revealed as a disguised Sherlock Holmes. In whispers he asks Watson to send Whitney home alone and wait outside so they can talk.

scenes.title: An Enemy and a Drive
scenes.summary: Outside the den Holmes laughs off suspicion of drug use, warns the den is a murder-trap tied to Neville St. Clair's disappearance, whistles for a dog-cart, and begins the long night drive toward Kent.

scenes.title: The Case of Neville St. Clair
scenes.summary: As they drive through London into the suburbs, Holmes lays out the St. Clair case: the cry at the window, the police search of the opium den, the blood, the clothes, the beggar Hugh Boone, and the coat stuffed with coins found in the Thames mud.

scenes.title: Arrival at Lee
scenes.summary: The carriage reaches the outskirts of Lee. Holmes points out the lighted Cedars and explains he is staying there to investigate, dreading facing Mrs. St. Clair with no news.

scenes.title: The Anxious Wife
scenes.summary: At the villa an anxious Mrs. St. Clair meets them at the door, sinks at Holmes's silent shake of the head, then warmly welcomes Watson inside.

scenes.title: A Letter From the Dead
scenes.summary: Over supper Mrs. St. Clair demands Holmes's plain opinion that her husband is dead, then stuns him by producing a letter received that day claiming to be from Neville himself.

scenes.title: Examining the Letter
scenes.summary: Holmes seizes the letter, noting the Gravesend postmark, mismatched ink, dirty thumb, tobacco-gummed flap, pencil writing, and enclosed signet-ring, while confirming the handwriting is her husband's hurried hand.

scenes.title: Alive or Dead
scenes.summary: Holmes cautions the letter may be forgery or delayed posting, but Mrs. St. Clair insists on a wife's sympathy that her husband lives, recalling how she sensed his minor cut on the day he vanished.

scenes.title: Cross-Examination
scenes.summary: Holmes closely questions her about the cry, the hands, the open window, the missing collar, and any talk of Swandam Lane or opium, establishing the key facts before supper and rest.

scenes.title: An All-Night Sitting in Smoke
scenes.summary: In their large double room Watson quickly falls asleep while Holmes, with an unsolved problem on his mind, prepares for an all-night sitting, building a divan of pillows and smoking shag tobacco motionless until sunrise.

scenes.title: Morning Light and the Key in the Bag
scenes.summary: At dawn Holmes wakes Watson cheerful and transformed, has the trap prepared, calls himself a fool, and declares he has found the key of the affair in the bathroom, now carried in his Gladstone bag, as they drive out into the morning.

scenes.title: Sunrise Drive to Bow Street
scenes.summary: Holmes confesses his blindness in the case as they gallop through the Surrey side at sunrise, crossing Waterloo Bridge to Bow Street where constables admit them.

scenes.title: Bradstreet and the Sleeping Prisoner
scenes.summary: Holmes asks Inspector Bradstreet for prisoner Boone, learns he is quiet but filthy, insists on taking his bag, and is led to the cell to see the beggar asleep.

scenes.title: The Beggar in the Bow Street Cell
scenes.summary: Holmes and Watson view the sleeping prisoner through the grating, noting his repulsive scar, twisted lip, and red hair. Holmes produces a bath-sponge and has the inspector quietly open the cell, then washes the prisoner's face.

scenes.title: Neville St. Clair Revealed
scenes.summary: The disguise peels away under the sponge to reveal Neville St. Clair alive, to the inspector's astonishment as he recognizes the missing man from his photograph.

scenes.title: Confession of the Beggar
scenes.summary: St. Clair confesses he was a journalist turned secret professional beggar as Hugh Boone, describes throwing his weighted coat into the Thames to hide his disguise, and the police agree to hush it up if Boone disappears forever.

scenes.title: A Trivial Problem by the Fire
scenes.summary: Watson visits Holmes after Christmas and finds him studying a battered old hat as an intellectual problem, insisting it involves no crime but curious deductions.

scenes.title: The Goose and the Hat
scenes.summary: Holmes recounts how Peterson found the hat and a Christmas goose dropped by Henry Baker after a street row on Tottenham Court Road.

scenes.title: What Can Be Gathered From a Hat
scenes.summary: Watson examines the hat and sees nothing, while Holmes declares the wearer highly intellectual, fallen in fortune, and affected by drink and domestic trouble.

scenes.title: The Deduction Explained
scenes.summary: Holmes explains his chain of inferences in detail — size, age, hat-securer, stains, hair, lime-cream, dust and tallow — to prove Baker's character and habits.

scenes.title: Treasure in the Crop
scenes.summary: Peterson rushes in to show a brilliant blue stone found in the goose's crop, which Holmes and Watson recognize as the stolen Countess of Morcar blue carbuncle lost at the Hotel Cosmopolitan with plumber John Horner accused.

scenes.title: Account of the Cosmopolitan Robbery
scenes.summary: Holmes reads the newspaper account of the Hotel Cosmopolitan jewel robbery, detailing the evidence against John Horner, his arrest, and referral to the Assizes.

scenes.title: A Plan to Find Henry Baker
scenes.summary: Holmes links jewel-case to goose to Henry Baker, places newspaper advertisements to lure him, and muses on the stone's bloody history while Watson leaves for his rounds.

scenes.title: Henry Baker Comes for His Hat
scenes.summary: Watson returns to Baker Street to find Henry Baker waiting outside. Holmes welcomes the large, shabby-genteel visitor, confirms the hat is his, and learns Baker did not advertise for his lost property for want of money, assuming roughs had taken both hat and goose.

scenes.title: The Fresh Goose and the Alpha Inn Club
scenes.summary: Holmes admits the original goose was eaten but offers a fresh replacement, which Baker gladly accepts while laughing off the leftover offal, convincing Holmes he knows nothing of the jewel. Asked its origin, Baker explains the Alpha Inn goose club run by Windigate before departing with hat and bird.

scenes.title: Night Walk to the Alpha Inn
scenes.summary: Holmes and Watson brave the frost to the Alpha Inn, learning its geese came not from the landlord but from Covent Garden salesman Breckinridge, with Horner's freedom at stake.

scenes.title: The Surly Salesman
scenes.summary: At Covent Garden Market Holmes questions a sold-out Breckinridge about the Alpha geese, provoking anger and evasiveness about his suppliers.

scenes.title: Won by a Wager
scenes.summary: Holmes tricks Breckinridge with a wager on town versus country breeding to consult his books, tracing the geese to Mrs. Oakshott of Brixton Road.

scenes.title: The Hubbub at the Goose Stall
scenes.summary: A hubbub erupts at Breckinridge's stall as the salesman furiously threatens a cringing rat-faced little man pestering him about geese and Mrs. Oakshott.

scenes.title: The Flight from Breckinridge
scenes.summary: Breckinridge drives the whining inquirer away into the darkness, and Holmes whispers that this may save a trip to Brixton Road before overtaking the frightened fellow.

scenes.title: The Offer in the Market-Place
scenes.summary: Holmes blandly offers assistance, proves he knows the whole chain of the geese from Mrs. Oakshott to Henry Baker, hails a cab, and rejects the man's alias of John Robinson.

scenes.title: The Unmasking of James Ryder
scenes.summary: The stranger confesses he is James Ryder, head attendant at the Hotel Cosmopolitan, and rides in tense silence with Holmes and Watson back to the sitting-room at Baker Street.

scenes.title: The Game's Up
scenes.summary: Back in Baker Street Holmes confronts Ryder with the white barred-tail goose and produces the carbuncle, accusing him of framing plumber Horner with Cusack's help.

scenes.title: The Stone Hidden in the Goose
scenes.summary: Ryder confesses that after Horner's arrest he fled to his sister Oakshott's fowl-yard in Brixton Road, thrust the stone down the throat of a fine white goose with a barred tail to smuggle it to his accomplice Maudsley in Kilburn, killed and carried off the wrong bird, and opened it to find no stone.

scenes.title: The Second Barred Tail
scenes.summary: Ryder tells how he rushed back to find the flock sold to Breckinridge of Covent Garden, learned there were two identical barred-tailed geese, failed to trace the right bird after Breckinridge sold the lot at once, and breaks down as a branded thief who never touched the wealth.

scenes.title: Season of Forgiveness
scenes.summary: Holmes lets the terrified Ryder flee rather than prosecute, reasoning Horner's case will collapse, in a season of forgiveness, before turning to another bird investigation.

scenes.title: An Early Morning Visitor in Terror
scenes.summary: Watson introduces the Roylott case as uniquely singular. Holmes wakes him early for an urgent young lady client in black, veiled and trembling with terror, setting a foreboding, mysterious mood.

scenes.title: Deductions from Ticket and Mud
scenes.summary: Holmes soothes the frightened visitor and dazzles with deductions from her return ticket and mud-spattered sleeve, proving her early drive by dog-cart to Leatherhead station.

scenes.title: The Roylott History and Cruel Stepfather
scenes.summary: Helen begs for help before her coming marriage; Holmes recalls Mrs. Farintosh. She recounts the ruined Roylott line, her mother's money, and her violent, gipsy-haunted stepfather with his cheetah and baboon.

scenes.title: Julia's Engagement and the Night Whistle
scenes.summary: Helen describes Julia's engagement, the three ground-floor bedrooms opening on one corridor, and Julia's unease about a low midnight whistle heard at 3 a.m., dismissed as gipsies.

scenes.title: Scream on the Wild Night
scenes.summary: Helen explains they always locked their doors for fear of Roylott's cheetah and baboon, then recounts the wild, sleepless night she heard Julia's scream followed by a whistle and metallic clang, found her convulsing in the passage crying of 'the speckled band' and pointing toward the Doctor's room, dying despite Roylott's and the doctor's aid.

scenes.title: Proof of the Locked Room
scenes.summary: Holmes questions Helen about the whistle, her sister's night-dress, the charred match and match-box in her hands, and the coroner's verdict: door fastened inside, barred shutters, solid walls and floor, stapled chimney, no violence, Julia alone and cause of death unfound.

scenes.title: Fear, Gipsies, and the Return of the Whistle
scenes.summary: No poison or violence found; coroner baffled. Helen suspects fear and a speckled gipsy band. Two years later, moved into Julia's bed for repairs, she hears the same herald whistle and flees to Holmes.

scenes.title: The Bruised Wrist and a Plan to Inspect
scenes.summary: Holmes accuses Helen of screening Roylott, revealing finger bruises on her wrist. He insists on inspecting Stoke Moran that day while Roylott is in London, and she departs to catch her train.

scenes.title: Theorizing the Gipsy Band
scenes.summary: Alone, Holmes and Watson debate the locked-room impossibility, whistles, marriage motive, gipsy band, and fallen shutter-bar, agreeing they must go to Stoke Moran to test objections.

scenes.title: The Violent Intrusion of Dr. Roylott
scenes.summary: Roylott bursts in, huge and furious, threatens Holmes as a meddler, bends a steel poker with bare hands. Holmes coolly straightens it after he storms out and orders breakfast and research.

scenes.title: A Motive in the Will and a Call to Arms
scenes.summary: Holmes returns with the deceased wife's will, showing Roylott would be crippled financially if the stepdaughters marry, giving him strong motive. He urges haste and asks Watson to bring his revolver before driving to Waterloo.

scenes.title: The Drive Through Surrey to Stoke Moran
scenes.summary: Holmes and Watson take the train to Leatherhead and drive through spring Surrey lanes to Stoke Moran, contrasting the peaceful country with their sinister quest, then leave the trap to meet Miss Stoner on foot.

scenes.title: Examination of House and Shutters
scenes.summary: Met by Helen, they tour the ruined manor. Holmes studies windows, corridor, and shutters, finds them impassable and the repair excuse suggestive, deepening the locked-room puzzle.

scenes.title: The Dummy Bell-Rope and Ventilator
scenes.summary: In the death chamber Holmes finds a dummy bell-rope unattached to wire hanging to the pillow, and a ventilator opening not outside but into Roylott's room, both suspiciously modern.

scenes.title: Milk, Safe, and Looped Lash
scenes.summary: Roylott's plain room yields a saucer of milk, iron safe of papers, chair worn by standing, and a looped dog-lash. Holmes turns grim, seeing enough of wicked cunning.

scenes.title: Orders for a Night Watch
scenes.summary: On the lawn Holmes orders Helen to spend the night in their room: signal with lamp, retreat to old room, leave the rest to them while they keep watch for the noise.

scenes.title: Waiting at the Inn and Deducing Danger
scenes.summary: From the Crown Inn they watch Roylott return in fury. Holmes warns of danger, explains he deduced the ventilator from cigar smoke, the clamped bed, rope as bridge, and a subtle horrible crime.

scenes.title: Stealing In and the Dreadful Vigil
scenes.summary: At eleven's lamp signal they cross dark grounds, startled by the baboon, slip shoeless into the bedroom, douse light, and endure a breathless hours-long vigil past three.

scenes.title: Hiss, Lash, and a Death Shriek
scenes.summary: A lantern gleam, oil smell, and hissing jet rouse Holmes to lash the bell-pull; a whistle, a piercing death shriek, then silence. They arm and enter Roylott's room to find him dead.

scenes.title: The Speckled Band Revealed
scenes.summary: The speckled band is revealed as a swamp adder coiled round Roylott's brow. Holmes cages it and later explains the vent-rope-bed train, milk training, whistle recall, and retribution.

scenes.title: A Problem Introduced by Watson
scenes.summary: Watson introduces the case as one of only two he brought to Holmes himself, recalling the summer of 1889 after his marriage when his Paddington practice was growing.

scenes.title: The Bloodied Morning Visitor
scenes.summary: Woken before seven for a railway case, Watson finds a pale young hydraulic engineer with a blood-soaked handkerchief, who unwraps a hand missing its thumb and laughs hysterically from shock.

scenes.title: A Murderous Attack
scenes.summary: Watson examines Hatherley's terrible, heavily bleeding wrist wound, which Hatherley says was made by something like a cleaver. Hatherley insists it was no accident but a murderous attack. Watson sponges, cleans, dresses, and bandages the wound while Hatherley bears it with fortitude.

scenes.title: Consult Sherlock Holmes
scenes.summary: Hatherley fears the police will not believe his extraordinary story without proof and that his vague clues will prevent justice. Watson urges him to bring the problem to his friend Sherlock Holmes before going to the official police.

scenes.title: A Cab to Baker Street
scenes.summary: Hatherley asks for an introduction to Holmes, Watson offers to take him round personally, calls a cab after telling his wife, and drives with his new acquaintance to Baker Street.

scenes.title: Reception Over Breakfast
scenes.summary: Holmes receives them in his dressing-gown over his before-breakfast pipe, orders fresh rashers and eggs, and after breakfast settles Hatherley on the sofa with brandy to tell his story.

scenes.title: The Struggling Engineer
scenes.summary: Hatherley recounts his lonely struggle as an orphan bachelor and hydraulic engineer, waiting daily in his Victoria Street chambers for two years with almost no work and only £27 10s in takings.

scenes.title: The Sinister Commission
scenes.summary: The cadaverously thin Colonel Lysander Stark arrives unannounced, flatters Hatherley for discretion, demands a promise of absolute secrecy, then springs to fling open the door to check the passage for eavesdropping clerks.

scenes.title: Fifty Guineas for a Night's Work
scenes.summary: Stark offers fifty guineas for a night's work, requiring a late train to Eyford in Berkshire and a seven-mile drive, and Hatherley, despite unease, accepts rather than lose the fee.

scenes.title: The Fuller's-Earth Story and the Midnight Drive
scenes.summary: Stark spins a tale of secret fuller's-earth and a hydraulic press, then Hatherley travels by midnight trains and a long silent carriage ride with frosted windows, while Holmes notes the fresh chestnut horse.

scenes.title: A Lamp in the Dark Passage
scenes.summary: Inside the pitch-dark house, Colonel Stark fetches a lamp as a beautiful woman in a rich dark dress appears with a light, startled by his gruff reply before he whispers to her and sends her back.

scenes.title: A Whispered Warning to Leave
scenes.summary: Left alone in a plain, silent room with German books and barred shutters, Hatherley grows uneasy until the frightened woman slips in to beg him in broken English to leave before it is too late, then vanishes at the sound of footsteps.

scenes.title: Inside the Hydraulic Press
scenes.summary: Stark and his thick, silent manager Ferguson lead Hatherley through a decaying labyrinth to the press chamber, where he diagnoses a leaking india-rubber band and realizes the metallic trough has nothing to do with fuller's-earth.

scenes.title: Death Closing From Above
scenes.summary: Challenged about the machine's true purpose, Hatherley is locked inside as the iron ceiling descends to crush him, and escapes only at the last instant through a sliding wooden wall panel.

scenes.title: The Leap and the Lost Thumb
scenes.summary: Guided by the woman down corridors, Hatherley jumps from a moonlit bedroom window, has his thumb severed by Stark's cleaver, faints among rose-bushes, and wakes to find house and garden vanished near Eyford Station.

scenes.title: Holmes Sees the Pattern
scenes.summary: Holmes produces a cutting about the vanished hydraulic engineer Jeremiah Hayling, declares Stark a desperate pirate-like criminal, and within hours the party boards a Reading train with Inspector Bradstreet.

scenes.title: The Circle on the Ordnance Map
scenes.summary: Bradstreet draws a ten-mile circle around Eyford while the companions argue north, south, east and west, until Holmes places his finger on the centre, exposing the twelve-mile drive as six out and six back, and names the gang as large-scale coiners.

scenes.title: Smoke Over Eyford Station
scenes.summary: Rolling into Eyford Station the party sees a huge column of smoke; the station-master tells them Dr. Becher's house broke out in the night and is now in a full blaze, and they hasten up the hill to find the whitewashed building spouting fire with three engines vainly fighting it.

scenes.title: Revenge and Flight to Reading
scenes.summary: Hatherley recognizes the gravel-drive, rose-bushes and window he jumped from; Holmes concludes his crushed oil-lamp set the wooden walls alight, and the German, Englishman and woman are never found, having been seen fleeing by cart toward Reading.

scenes.title: Ashes and Experience
scenes.summary: Firemen discover a severed thumb, ruined coining machinery, and stores of nickel and tin, while mould shows Hatherley was carried to safety, leaving him to rue his lost thumb and fee as Holmes laughs of experience gained.

scenes.title: A Letter from a Noble Client
scenes.summary: Watson introduces the St. Simon scandal and recalls a rainy afternoon in Baker Street when Holmes receives a noble letter requesting help, prompting them to gather newspaper background before the 4 o'clock client visit.

scenes.title: Society Papers and the Arranged Wedding
scenes.summary: Watson reads society notices tracing Lord St. Simon's engagement to Californian heiress Hatty Doran, the quiet wedding at Hanover Square, and the honeymoon plan, establishing money and transatlantic stakes.

scenes.title: Singular Occurrence at the Breakfast
scenes.summary: The report turns sensational: the bride vanished from the Lancaster Gate breakfast after a disturbance by Flora Millar, with arrest rumours and foul play, sharply exciting Holmes's interest as the client's ring sounds.

scenes.title: Enter Lord St. Simon
scenes.summary: Lord St. Simon arrives in foppish, aggrieved dignity and Holmes opens his examination, confirming the press account and beginning direct questioning about the courtship.

scenes.title: The Californian Heiress Described
scenes.summary: St. Simon describes meeting Hatty in San Francisco, her mining-camp tomboy nature, volcanic resolve, and underlying nobility, while Holmes studies her ivory miniature.

scenes.title: The Dropped Bouquet in the Pew
scenes.summary: Questioning focuses on the wedding morning: bright spirits, then abrupt temper over a dropped bouquet returned by a common stranger in the pew, a trifle Holmes finds highly significant.

scenes.title: Jumping a Claim and Flight
scenes.summary: St. Simon recounts the maid Alice's brief talk about 'jumping a claim,' the solitary entry to breakfast, sudden apology and flight upstairs in ulster and bonnet into Hyde Park.

scenes.title: The Former Dancer and a Solved Case
scenes.summary: St. Simon explains Flora Millar's jealous threats and Lestrade's decoy theory, offers nervous derangement as his own excuse, then is stunned when Holmes declares the case already solved and demands his wife's whereabouts.

scenes.title: Holmes Is Certain, Lestrade Arrives Wet
scenes.summary: Amused at his own certainty citing parallel cases in Aberdeen and Munich, Holmes welcomes a damp, dissatisfied Lestrade fresh from outdoor inquiry.

scenes.title: Clothes from the Serpentine
scenes.summary: Lestrade reports dragging the Serpentine for Lady St. Simon's body and triumphantly dumps water-soaked wedding dress, shoes, veil and ring found floating near the margin.

scenes.title: The Note and the Hotel Bill
scenes.summary: Lestrade brandishes a pencilled lure signed F.H.M. as proof against Flora, but Holmes seizes on the reverse hotel bill and cryptically tells him Lady St. Simon is a myth before Lestrade storms out.

scenes.title: Holmes Out and a Supper Appears
scenes.summary: Holmes slips out for outdoor work, and Watson is astonished when a lavish epicurean cold supper for five is delivered and laid out in their lodgings.

scenes.title: An Expectant Return
scenes.summary: Holmes returns expectant of company, and Lord St. Simon hurries in startled by Holmes's message, dreading humiliation for the Duke's family.

scenes.title: The True Wedding Revealed
scenes.summary: Holmes ushers in Mr. and Mrs. Francis Hay Moulton — the missing bride and her first husband — who recount their California engagement, secret marriage, his reported death by Apaches, her second wedding, the pew note, and cab escape to Gordon Square.

scenes.title: Cold Forgiveness and Departure
scenes.summary: Unmoved, Lord St. Simon refuses public discussion and forgiveness, coldly shakes her hand, declines supper, and stalks out, leaving Holmes to offer American hospitality instead.

scenes.title: How Simple When Explained
scenes.summary: Alone, Holmes explains his exclusion-chain from willing bride to American lover-husband, how hotel prices and the bill led him to Gordon Square, and closes the bleak autumn evening by reaching for his violin.

scenes.title: The Madman Seen from the Window
scenes.summary: On a bright, crisp snowy February morning Watson looks from the bow-window down Baker Street and spots a tall, portly, richly dressed gentleman of fifty running hard, jerking his hands and contorting his face like a madman, while Holmes rises to observe over his shoulder.

scenes.title: The Despairing Client Bursts In
scenes.summary: Holmes declares the frantic man is coming to consult him professionally, and moments later the puffing visitor rushes in, speechless with grief and despair, plucking his hair and beating his head against the wall until Holmes and Watson pull him away and Holmes soothes him into the easy-chair.

scenes.title: The Banker's Shame
scenes.summary: Holmes soothes the visitor into telling his story. The man reveals himself as Alexander Holder of Holder & Stevenson, a foremost London banker brought to despair by sudden public disgrace and private affliction.

scenes.title: The Loan and the Coronet
scenes.summary: Holder explains his business in loans on security and how an exalted, unnamed client urgently borrowed £50,000 for four days, leaving the priceless Beryl Coronet with thirty-nine beryls as pledge under strict secrecy.

scenes.title: The Coronet Carried to Streatham
scenes.summary: Fearing to leave the national treasure in the office safe, Holder carries the beryl coronet case home to Streatham and locks it in his dressing-room bureau, then describes his out-sleeping groom and page and his maid-servants, including the pretty new second waiting-maid Lucy Parr.

scenes.title: A Son Lost and a Niece Cherished
scenes.summary: Holder describes his small family: his widowed indulgence of his wild, gambling son Arthur, Arthur's fascinating but deeply distrusted friend Sir George Burnwell, and his adopted niece Mary, his devoted housekeeper who has twice refused Arthur's proposal.

scenes.title: The Evening Before the Crime
scenes.summary: Over coffee Holder mentions the coronet. Arthur asks where it is and later begs for £200 to pay club debts, is refused and leaves angry. Holder secures the house and finds Mary has fastened a window after seeing maid Lucy slip in from outside.

scenes.title: Caught in the Night
scenes.summary: Awakened at 2 a.m., Holder finds Arthur in his shirt holding the coronet with a corner and three beryls missing. Arthur refuses explanation, is accused of theft, and despite pleas is given into police custody after a fruitless search.

scenes.title: Holmes Doubts the Obvious
scenes.summary: Holmes questions Holder closely, arguing Arthur's supposed actions are untenable and the coronet could not be broken silently. He notes Mary's shock and insists on seeing Streatham himself to look deeper than police.

scenes.title: The Journey to Fairbank
scenes.summary: Watson eagerly accompanies Holmes and the banker to Fairbank by rail and on foot, convinced of Arthur's guilt but hopeful because Holmes is unsatisfied; Holmes rides in silent thought while Holder takes heart and chats.

scenes.title: Holmes Walks the Grounds
scenes.summary: At the white stone house, Holmes leaves Holder and Watson at the door to walk slowly round the front, tradesmen's path, garden, and stable lane in the snow; while they wait by the dining-room fire, pale, grief-stricken Mary Holder enters and caresses her uncle.

scenes.title: Mary Pleads for Arthur
scenes.summary: Mary pleads that Arthur is innocent and begs her uncle to liberate him and let the matter drop, but Holder insists on probing it until the gems are found and reveals he brought investigators from London; she turns to Watson, then meets the snow-covered Holmes returning from the stable lane and asks him questions to help clear Arthur.

scenes.title: Clues in Snow and Glass
scenes.summary: Holmes probes Mary about locked windows and Lucy's sweetheart. He deduces the lover waits up the path and has a wooden leg, astonishing her, then examines the lower windows, especially the hall window onto the stable lane.

scenes.title: The Bureau and the Broken Corner
scenes.summary: Upstairs Holmes tests the bureau lock and the coronet's strength, proving it could not be torn quietly by one man. Learning Arthur was barefoot, he leaves alone for an hour to study footmarks outside.

scenes.title: Holmes Withholds His Conclusions
scenes.summary: Holmes finishes his solitary examination in the snow and remains inscrutable, refusing to tell Holder where the gems are. He secures carte blanche and arranges a morning meeting at Baker Street, then returns home with Watson and quickly disguises himself as a common loafer.

scenes.title: On the Trail to Streatham
scenes.summary: Disguised, Holmes sets out on his trail, taking only a makeshift sandwich. He returns briefly in excellent spirits with an old elastic-sided boot, mentions Streatham, then leaves again for the West End. Watson waits until midnight, finding Holmes fresh over coffee in the morning.

scenes.title: The Despair of the Banker
scenes.summary: A haggard and aged-looking Holder arrives early and reports fresh disaster: his niece Mary has vanished overnight without sleeping in her bed, leaving a farewell note saying she has brought trouble upon him, must leave forever, and must not be searched for, prompting Holder to fear suicide.

scenes.title: The Return of the Beryls
scenes.summary: Holmes dismisses suicide and declares Holder's troubles nearing an end, bargains the recovery price up to a £4000 cheque, then produces the missing triangular gold corner set with three beryls, which Holder seizes with passionate joy and relief.

scenes.title: The Tool and the Witness
scenes.summary: Holmes demands Holder apologize to Arthur, reveals Mary became Burnwell's tool, and reconstructs how she passed the coronet through the stable window while Arthur watched hidden behind the curtain.

scenes.title: The Struggle in the Snow
scenes.summary: Arthur chased Burnwell barefoot through the snow, struggled for the coronet, cut Burnwell over the eye, and broke the coronet before rushing back to straighten it.

scenes.title: The Father's Remorse
scenes.summary: Holder grasps Arthur's chivalrous silence to protect Mary, understands her faint and his plea for five minutes, and laments how cruelly he misjudged his son.

scenes.title: Deduction and Recovery
scenes.summary: Holmes details his snow-track deduction, exclusion of maids, identification of Burnwell, purchase of his shoes, pistol confrontation, and buying back the stones from a receiver. Holder thanks him and learns Mary has fled with Burnwell to her ruin.

scenes.title: In Praise of Trifles
scenes.summary: Tossing aside the Telegraph, Holmes tells Watson that to the lover of art for its own sake the keenest pleasure lies in trifling cases that allow deduction and logical synthesis, and reproves him for embellishing his records with colour and life instead of severe reasoning from cause to effect.

scenes.title: The Days of Great Cases Past
scenes.summary: On a foggy spring morning in Baker Street after breakfast, Holmes answers Watson's hurt reply by insisting crime is common but logic is rare, calls his records tales instead of lectures, laments that the days of great cases are past and his practice has sunk to lost pencils and schoolgirls, then tosses over the morning's crumpled letter as his zero-point.

scenes.title: The Governess Letter
scenes.summary: Holmes shares Violet Hunter's letter asking advice about a governess post; as half-past ten strikes, they anticipate her arrival, hoping a whim may prove serious.

scenes.title: An Offer Too Good
scenes.summary: Violet Hunter arrives and explains her destitution after Colonel Munro left for America; at Westaway's agency a smiling stout man offers her an astonishing 100 pounds a year.

scenes.title: The Price of Hair
scenes.summary: Rucastle advances pay but demands odd obedience, wearing his whims and cutting her chestnut hair short; when she refuses, he withdraws the offer and she is shown out.

scenes.title: Reconsideration and Warning
scenes.summary: Regretting her refusal, Hunter receives Rucastle's raised offer of 120 pounds with electric-blue dress and hair conditions; Holmes warns the pay is too good and the household seems unfit.

scenes.title: A Promise of Protection
scenes.summary: Holmes promises help by telegram day or night if she is in danger; Hunter leaves resolved to sacrifice her hair, while Holmes gravely expects to hear from her soon.

scenes.title: Summons to Winchester
scenes.summary: A fortnight later a late-night urgent telegram from Hunter summons them to Winchester; they consult Bradshaw and take the half-past nine train.

scenes.title: The Bright Hampshire Spring
scenes.summary: By eleven the next morning Holmes and Watson are travelling toward Winchester, Holmes reading papers until the Hampshire border, then admiring the bright ideal spring scenery of blue sky, sunshine, and farmsteads among new foliage.

scenes.title: The Horror of the Lonely Houses
scenes.summary: Watson admires the fresh beauty of the scattered houses, but Holmes gravely reflects on their isolation and impunity for hidden cruelty, contrasting town sympathy and justice with lonely country houses, noting Miss Hunter has freedom yet danger lies in the five miles of country, and that he has seven explanations awaiting her account at Winchester.

scenes.title: Life at the Copper Beeches
scenes.summary: At the Black Swan, Hunter reports no ill-treatment but unease; she describes Copper Beeches, the pale wife, cruel child, unpleasant servants, and being made to wear the blue dress and sit laughing in the window.

scenes.title: The Watcher in the Road
scenes.summary: Hunter tells how the window sitting was repeated and again cut short mid-reading, how she hid a shard of hand-mirror to see behind her and spotted a small bearded man in grey watching from Southampton Road, and how Mrs. Rucastle caught her and had the blind drawn, ending the window performances.

scenes.title: The Mastiff Unleashed
scenes.summary: Rucastle shows Hunter the chained mastiff Carlo in the outhouse and warns that groom Toller alone controls him and lets him loose at night, a warning confirmed when she sees the giant tawny dog patrolling the moonlit lawn.

scenes.title: The Locked Hair and the Forbidden Wing
scenes.summary: Violet Hunter finds an identical coil of her own cut hair locked in her chest drawer, surveys an uninhabited wing locked by an enraged Rucastle, notes its dirty and shuttered windows dismissed as his photographic dark room, and slips through the forbidden door when it is left unlocked.

scenes.title: The Shadow Under the Barricaded Door
scenes.summary: Inside the bare passage she finds empty dusty rooms and a centre door barricaded with an iron bed-bar yet lit from within, hears pacing and sees a shadow pass under the door, and flees in terror into the arms of the waiting Rucastle.

scenes.title: Threat and Flight
scenes.summary: Caught by a smiling then raging Rucastle who threatens to throw her to the mastiff, Hunter flees to wire Holmes from the village office while Toller is drunk.

scenes.title: Holmes's Impersonation Theory
scenes.summary: Holmes deduces Hunter was hired to impersonate imprisoned Alice to deceive her fiance, and plots a seven o'clock return with Mrs. Toller locked in the wine-cellar.

scenes.title: The Empty Prison
scenes.summary: Arriving at sunset they lock Mrs. Toller below, break into the silent empty prison with open skylight and ladder, and are confronted by a stick-wielding Rucastle.

scenes.title: Loosed Hunger
scenes.summary: Rucastle rushes for the starved dog; its baying turns to screams as it mauls his throat, and Watson shoots it before they carry the mangled man to the sofa.

scenes.title: Mrs. Toller's Confession
scenes.summary: Freed from the cellar, Mrs. Toller confesses that Alice was slighted after her father's remarriage, pressed to sign away her own money, fell into brain-fever and lost her hair, was then kept prisoner, and that Miss Hunter was brought down to deter the persistent Mr. Fowler, whom Toller agreed to help.

scenes.title: Solution and Aftermath
scenes.summary: Holmes confirms Fowler bribed the Tollers with drink and a ready ladder for escape while Rucastle was out, closes the case, and Watson relates the aftermath: Rucastle left broken and nursed by his wife, Fowler married to Alice in Southampton with a Mauritius appointment, and Hunter become head of a school at Walsall.
